Screaming fandom isn’t necessarily a sign that a show works, however, which has always been the essential trouble with Heathers, which was wibbly-wobbly enough as a movie, its cutting putdowns well-remembered and its convoluted plotting forgotten.
A cautionary fable from Gen X to Gen Z, Heathers is the great musical of our nihilistic age, when so many people look at the world as it is and want to burn it down.
Sharper, sleeker, and eerily timely, the revival proves that what began as a cult curiosity has grown into one of the best stage musicals of the last decade.
If Heathers the Musical seemed too cynical in 2014 when it also played at New World Stages, time or events have caught up with it and it now seems a reflection of the life we live.
Her comedic snark matched with a killer voice is as near to musical theatre perfection as you can get.
Above all -- and perhaps most importantly -- the show boasts more talent per square foot than almost any other show in New York City.
Happily, you needn’t consider any of this to enjoy the mischievous fun that “Heathers The Musical” provides.
Beyond its sociological themes, Heathers is a ton of stylish, well-crafted fun with top-notch acting and top-to-bottom earworms.
This Heathers: The Musical revival might struggle to bleed as the material requires.
Whatever Heathers: The Musical (New World Stages, booking to Jan. 25, 2026) is as a piece of theater, it is being fiercely embraced by its dedicated fan base as a phenomenon.
As fans of the movie know, "Heathers" goes into much darker territory, and this is where the musical loses its way, failing to find a tone that can encompass spoofiness, social satire and depravity.

Andy Fickman’s production and the softening revisions Kevin Murphy and Laurence O’Keefe have made to the book and score add up to a tepid, if tuneful adaptation of what was once a controversial, giddily violent send-up of teen culture.

Yet the pastel-colored Off-Broadway production could easily pass for a bubbly high school musical comedy, with its pleasantly poppy score, fun and sometimes clever lyrics, and a principal cast full of bright young Broadway talent.
Heathers the Musical is fun and silly but treats its all-too-real subject a bit too lightly and easily.
Even tastelessness can leave a bad taste in your mouth.
The myriad reasons to see (and hear!) Heathers are small in number, whereas the myriad reasons not to see (and hear!) it—unless you’re a Corn Nut—are much larger.
Simply put, Heathers: The Musical is a must-see.
Heathers’s truth is powerful and engaging, and the experience of seeing it is an absolute delight.
What we end up with is an examination of the social terrors of suburban upper middle class high school that continually pokes fun at itself.
Heathers is still speaking loud and clear.

As a whole, the revival of Heathers the Musical exceeds expectations with its commitment to the source material and to its initial fan base, as well as to the numerous aficionados who have come on board since its decade off the stage.
Heathers the Musical pulls off that rare thing: indulging our craving for nostalgia and camp while also bringing fresh perspectives to familiar tropes.
From the moment the first lyrics are delivered, more shouted than sung (“Freak! Slut! Burn-Out! Bug-Eyes! Poser! Hard Ass!”), you’re in for a bit of time travel that’s well worth the trip.
I enjoyed “Heathers The Musical.” It’s often funny, and engaging, but troubling, nevertheless.
The result, under the breakneck direction of Andy Fickman, is that there is something for everyone, but little that feels sincere.
I can’t say that I found Heathers satisfying musical theatre in any real sense, but I greatly enjoyed the crowd’s enthusiasm...
A high-gloss revival with a powerhouse cast that nearly distracts from a musical more interested in fan service than subversion.
Overall, “Heathers: The Musical” is lighthearted, engaging, and thoroughly entertaining.
The show demonstrates strong self-awareness and understanding of its comedic appeal, creating an entertaining evening when performance and audience interaction align effectively.

cn.t: Critics find this revival sharper and more timely than its 2014 debut, praising the energetic performances and rock-concert atmosphere, though some note tonal struggles between dark satire and earnest messaging in adapting the cult film.

vr.q: Easily the best production of Heathers I've seen, and that really, truly is due to this cast.

This is really a great show. The music is very exciting and smart and clever. The performances are excellent... if Heather's sounds like your kind of twisted fun, head to New World Stages and check it out.
